institution: ICMR multicentric ESBL study (AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER, CMC Vellore, JIPMER)

verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Overall figures were derived by pooling the Table III resistant counts (ESBL plus non-ESBL) per drug, for example E. coli amikacin 8/167 + 75/202 = 83/369 resistant, giving 77.5% susceptible. Table II gives % susceptible for each centre separately. ESBL was detected by the combined disc test. K. pneumoniae pooled denominators are at most 224, below the 304 isolates collected.

notes: Gautam et al. (Indian J Med Res 2019) report an ICMR study of ESBL at four tertiary centres (AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry), October 2014 to March 2016: E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304) from blood, pus, sputum and body fluids, tested by Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion with CLSI breakpoints. Figures pool the resistant counts given separately for ESBL and non-ESBL isolates and show 100 minus %R, so intermediate counts as susceptible; colistin is the overall susceptibility printed in the text (E. coli 271 of 274, K. pneumoniae 229 of 234). For E. coli the pooled denominators reach 369, more than the 341 isolates collected. Some drugs were tested on far fewer isolates (E. coli ertapenem 90, cefpodoxime 68). ESBL was detected in 33% of E. coli (98 of 298) and 42% of K. pneumoniae (102 of 245).
